title: Free tags for Pods and networks
goal: Label Pods and networks with free tags and give them short names without repeated context.
summary: Every Pod and network gets up to eight free tags. Network tags also apply to its members on screen without being copied. The Automatisierungen view filters by tags, Codex can set and find them, and inbox items show them. Existing names lose their context prefixes; tags and the network carry that context.

problem.statement: 15 of 20 active Pods repeat a context in their name, such as "Delta Mind ·" or "Morgenbriefing ·", because Pods has no way to label a company or topic.
problem.impact: Names are long and similar, lists are hard to scan, and Pods of one company cannot be shown together.
problem.approach: Store free tags like automation descriptions, inherit network tags in the view, filter by tag, add network renaming and shorten the existing names.
problem.outcome: Short names, one filter per company or topic, and the same tags in the desktop, browser, Codex and inbox.

milestones.title: Tags in the workspace
milestones.goal: Store and publish free tags for Pods and networks.
acceptance: A Pod or network has 0–8 tags; a tag is trimmed, lowercased, 1–32 characters of letters, digits and hyphens, unique per item.
Tags are set with one revisioned workspace command, like descriptions, locally and through the central workspace; a stale revision is refused.
The workspace view lists each item's own tags and, for network members, the inherited network tags separately; nothing is copied.
milestones.rollback: Restore the paired profile backup; tags are an additive table.

milestones.title: Show, edit and filter
milestones.goal: Tags appear wherever Pods and networks are listed.
acceptance: Automatisierungen (desktop and browser) shows tags as chips and has a tag filter with suggestions from existing tags; a network filter includes its members.
Tags are edited in the settings of a Pod or network with suggestions; the filter choice is remembered per device.
Codex sets tags and lists Pods and networks by tag through the MCP workspace tool.
milestones.rollback: Hide the chips and filter; stored tags stay.

milestones.title: Rename networks and shorten names
milestones.goal: Remove repeated context from the existing names.
acceptance: A network can be renamed without a new network revision; members, history and decisions keep their identity.
Where two items share a short name, lists show the network beside it.
The renaming table in this plan is applied live after the release, with tags set before names change.
milestones.rollback: Rename back from the table; nothing depends on the display names.

milestones.title: Release and verify
milestones.goal: Roll out relay first, then the signed desktop, then apply the renaming.
acceptance: Relay and signed desktop installed with a paired backup; all Pods keep running.
Screenshots of Automatisierungen with chips and an active filter are inspected; the owner checks names and tags.
Evidence is published as a Test Run.
milestones.rollback: Restore the paired backup and the previous relay image; rename back.

decisions.title: Free tags
decisions.description: Any tag may be used; the editor suggests existing ones so spellings converge.

decisions.title: Rename in the same change
decisions.description: The existing Pods and networks get short names as listed below.

decisions.title: Groups stay structure, tags are labels
decisions.description: Groups keep holding network members on the map; tags never move Pods. Network tags are inherited in the view, never copied (no divergent copies).

risks.title: Short names collide
risks.mitigation: Lists show the network beside a shared name; Pods are always addressed by id.

risks.title: Tag spellings drift
risks.mitigation: Normalization plus suggestions; a tag can be renamed for all items in one step later if needed.

sections.title: Deferred
sections.body: Deferred during implementation on October 11, 2026, and reported to the owner: tags in portable export and import (the package format in pods-protocol needs its own versioned feature) and tags on inbox items in the phone app. The desktop and browser show tags everywhere Pods and networks are listed.
